prometheus.interval: Auto-calculated interval based on time range and resolution (ex. "15s", "5m", "1h")
prometheus.range: Duration of the selected time range
prometheus.rate-interval: Safe interval for rate() and increase(), adjusts to scrape frequency

keywords.with: Defines templates that the query after it can use.
keywords.keep-metric-names: Keeps the metric names that the function or operator would drop.
keywords.limit: Returns up to the given number of groups.
keywords.if: Returns the left side only where the right side has a value.
keywords.ifnot: Returns the left side only where the right side has no value.
keywords.default: Fills the gaps in the left side with the right side.

rollup.absent-over-time: Returns 1 if the window has no samples.
rollup.aggr-over-time: Calculates several of the listed rollup functions over the window at once.
rollup.ascent-over-time: Calculates how much the sample values rose over the window.
rollup.avg-over-time: Calculates the average of the samples in the window.
rollup.changes: Counts how many times the sample value changed in the window.
rollup.changes-prometheus: Counts how many times the sample value changed in the window, ignoring the sample just before it, as Prometheus does.
rollup.count-eq-over-time: Counts the samples in the window that equal the given value.
rollup.count-gt-over-time: Counts the samples in the window that are bigger than the given value.
rollup.count-le-over-time: Counts the samples in the window that do not exceed the given value.
rollup.count-ne-over-time: Counts the samples in the window that differ from the given value.
rollup.count-over-time: Counts the samples in the window.
rollup.count-values-over-time: Counts the samples with the same value in the window, one series per value under the given label.
rollup.decreases-over-time: Counts how many times the sample value went down in the window.
rollup.default-rollup: Returns the last sample value in the window.
rollup.delta: Calculates the difference between the last sample before the window and the last sample in it.
rollup.delta-prometheus: Calculates the difference between the first and the last sample in the window, as Prometheus does.
rollup.deriv: Calculates the per-second derivative over the window with linear regression.
rollup.deriv-fast: Calculates the per-second derivative from the first and the last sample in the window.
rollup.descent-over-time: Calculates how much the sample values fell over the window.
rollup.distinct-over-time: Counts the unique sample values in the window.
rollup.duration-over-time: Returns how many seconds the series was present in the window.
rollup.first-over-time: Returns the first sample value in the window.
rollup.geomean-over-time: Calculates the geometric mean of the samples in the window.
rollup.histogram-over-time: Builds a VictoriaMetrics histogram from the samples in the window.
rollup.hoeffding-bound-lower: Calculates the lower Hoeffding bound for the given confidence over the samples in the window.
rollup.hoeffding-bound-upper: Calculates the upper Hoeffding bound for the given confidence over the samples in the window.
rollup.holt-winters: Smooths the samples in the window with double exponential smoothing, using the given smoothing and trend factors.
rollup.idelta: Calculates the difference between the last two samples in the window.
rollup.ideriv: Calculates the per-second derivative from the last two samples in the window.
rollup.increase: Calculates how much a counter increased over the window.
rollup.increase-prometheus: Calculates how much a counter increased over the window, ignoring the sample just before it, as Prometheus does.
rollup.increase-pure: Calculates how much a counter increased over the window, assuming every counter starts at 0.
rollup.increases-over-time: Counts how many times the sample value went up in the window.
rollup.integrate: Calculates the integral of the samples over the window.
rollup.irate: Calculates the per-second rate from the last two samples in the window.
rollup.lag: Returns the seconds between the last sample and the current point.
rollup.last-over-time: Returns the last sample value in the window.
rollup.lifetime: Returns the seconds between the first and the last sample in the window.
rollup.mad-over-time: Calculates the median absolute deviation of the samples in the window.
rollup.max-over-time: Returns the biggest sample value in the window.
rollup.median-over-time: Calculates the median of the samples in the window.
rollup.min-over-time: Returns the smallest sample value in the window.
rollup.mode-over-time: Returns the most frequent sample value in the window.
rollup.outlier-iqr-over-time: Returns the last sample if it lies outside the interquartile range of the window.
rollup.predict-linear: Predicts the value the given number of seconds ahead with linear regression over the window.
rollup.present-over-time: Returns 1 if the window has at least one sample.
rollup.quantile-over-time: Calculates the given quantile of the samples in the window.
rollup.quantiles-over-time: Calculates several quantiles of the samples in the window, one series per quantile under the given label.
rollup.range-over-time: Calculates the difference between the biggest and the smallest sample in the window.
rollup.rate: Calculates the average per-second rate at which a counter increased over the window.
rollup.rate-prometheus: Calculates the average per-second rate at which a counter increased over the window, ignoring the sample just before it, as Prometheus does.
rollup.rate-over-sum: Calculates the per-second rate of the sum of the samples in the window.
rollup.resets: Counts the counter resets in the window.
rollup.rollup: Returns the minimum, maximum and average of the samples in the window, each as a series with a rollup label.
rollup.rollup-candlestick: Returns the open, high, low and close values of the window, each as a series with a rollup label.
rollup.rollup-delta: Returns the minimum, maximum and average difference between adjacent samples, each as a series with a rollup label.
rollup.rollup-deriv: Returns the minimum, maximum and average per-second derivative between adjacent samples, each as a series with a rollup label.
rollup.rollup-increase: Returns the minimum, maximum and average increase between adjacent samples, each as a series with a rollup label.
rollup.rollup-rate: Returns the minimum, maximum and average per-second rate between adjacent samples, each as a series with a rollup label.
rollup.rollup-scrape-interval: Returns the minimum, maximum and average seconds between adjacent samples, each as a series with a rollup label.
rollup.scrape-interval: Calculates the average seconds between the samples in the window.
rollup.share-eq-over-time: Returns the share of samples in the window that equal the given value, from 0 to 1.
rollup.share-gt-over-time: Returns the share of samples in the window that are bigger than the given value, from 0 to 1.
rollup.share-le-over-time: Returns the share of samples in the window that do not exceed the given value, from 0 to 1.
rollup.stale-samples-over-time: Counts the staleness markers in the window.
rollup.stddev-over-time: Calculates the standard deviation of the samples in the window.
rollup.stdvar-over-time: Calculates the variance of the samples in the window.
rollup.sum-eq-over-time: Sums the samples in the window that equal the given value.
rollup.sum-gt-over-time: Sums the samples in the window that are bigger than the given value.
rollup.sum-le-over-time: Sums the samples in the window that do not exceed the given value.
rollup.sum-over-time: Sums the samples in the window.
rollup.sum2-over-time: Sums the squares of the samples in the window.
rollup.tfirst-over-time: Returns the timestamp of the first sample in the window, in seconds.
rollup.timestamp: Returns the timestamp of the last sample in the window, in seconds.
rollup.timestamp-with-name: Returns the timestamp of the last sample in the window, in seconds, and keeps the metric name.
rollup.tlast-change-over-time: Returns the timestamp of the last change in the window, in seconds.
rollup.tlast-over-time: Returns the timestamp of the last sample in the window, in seconds. The same as timestamp.
rollup.tmax-over-time: Returns the timestamp of the biggest sample in the window, in seconds.
rollup.tmin-over-time: Returns the timestamp of the smallest sample in the window, in seconds.
rollup.zscore-over-time: Calculates the z-score of the samples in the window.

transform.abs: Returns the absolute value of each point.
transform.absent: Returns 1 if the query returns no points.
transform.acos: Returns the inverse cosine of each point.
transform.acosh: Returns the inverse hyperbolic cosine of each point.
transform.asin: Returns the inverse sine of each point.
transform.asinh: Returns the inverse hyperbolic sine of each point.
transform.atan: Returns the inverse tangent of each point.
transform.atanh: Returns the inverse hyperbolic tangent of each point.
transform.bitmap-and: Returns the bitwise AND of each point and the given mask.
transform.bitmap-or: Returns the bitwise OR of each point and the given mask.
transform.bitmap-xor: Returns the bitwise XOR of each point and the given mask.
transform.buckets-limit: Limits the number of histogram buckets to the given number.
transform.ceil: Rounds each point up to the nearest integer.
transform.clamp: Keeps each point between the given minimum and maximum.
transform.clamp-max: Keeps each point at or below the given maximum.
transform.clamp-min: Keeps each point at or above the given minimum.
transform.cos: Returns the cosine of each point.
transform.cosh: Returns the hyperbolic cosine of each point.
transform.day-of-month: Returns the day of the month of each point.
transform.day-of-week: Returns the day of the week of each point, from 0 for Sunday.
transform.day-of-year: Returns the day of the year of each point.
transform.days-in-month: Returns the number of days in the month of each point.
transform.deg: Converts each point from radians to degrees.
transform.drop-empty-series: Drops the series that have no points.
transform.end: Returns the timestamp of the last point, in seconds.
transform.exp: Returns e raised to the power of each point.
transform.floor: Rounds each point down to the nearest integer.
transform.histogram-avg: Calculates the average from histogram buckets.
transform.histogram-fraction: Calculates the share of observations between the given bounds from histogram buckets.
transform.histogram-quantile: Calculates the given quantile from histogram buckets.
transform.histogram-quantiles: Calculates several quantiles from histogram buckets, one series per quantile under the given label.
transform.histogram-share: Calculates the share of observations below the given bound from histogram buckets.
transform.histogram-stddev: Calculates the standard deviation from histogram buckets.
transform.histogram-stdvar: Calculates the variance from histogram buckets.
transform.hour: Returns the hour of each point.
transform.interpolate: Fills gaps with values interpolated between the points around them.
transform.keep-last-value: Fills gaps with the last value before them.
transform.keep-next-value: Fills gaps with the next value after them.
transform.limit-offset: Skips the given number of series and returns up to the given number of the rest.
transform.ln: Returns the natural logarithm of each point.
transform.log10: Returns the base 10 logarithm of each point.
transform.log2: Returns the base 2 logarithm of each point.
transform.minute: Returns the minute of each point.
transform.month: Returns the month of each point.
transform.now: Returns the current timestamp, in seconds.
transform.prometheus-buckets: Converts VictoriaMetrics histogram buckets with vmrange labels into Prometheus buckets with le labels.
transform.rad: Converts each point from degrees to radians.
transform.rand: Returns random numbers between 0 and 1 with an even distribution.
transform.rand-exponential: Returns random numbers with an exponential distribution.
transform.rand-normal: Returns random numbers with a normal distribution.
transform.range-avg: Calculates the average of the points across the time range.
transform.range-first: Returns the first point in the time range.
transform.range-last: Returns the last point in the time range.
transform.range-linear-regression: Fits a straight line through the points across the time range.
transform.range-mad: Calculates the median absolute deviation of the points across the time range.
transform.range-max: Returns the biggest point across the time range.
transform.range-median: Calculates the median of the points across the time range.
transform.range-min: Returns the smallest point across the time range.
transform.range-normalize: Scales the points of each series to the range from 0 to 1.
transform.range-quantile: Calculates the given quantile of the points across the time range.
transform.range-stddev: Calculates the standard deviation of the points across the time range.
transform.range-stdvar: Calculates the variance of the points across the time range.
transform.range-sum: Sums the points across the time range.
transform.range-trim-outliers: Drops the points farther from the median than the given multiple of the median absolute deviation.
transform.range-trim-spikes: Drops the given share of the biggest spikes.
transform.range-trim-zscore: Drops the points farther from the average than the given multiple of the standard deviation.
transform.range-zscore: Calculates the z-score of each point across the time range.
transform.remove-resets: Removes counter resets, so the counter keeps rising.
transform.round: Rounds each point to the nearest integer, or to the nearest multiple of the given number.
transform.ru: Calculates resource utilization from 0 to 100% from the free and the maximum amount.
transform.running-avg: Calculates the running average of the points.
transform.running-max: Calculates the running maximum of the points.
transform.running-min: Calculates the running minimum of the points.
transform.running-sum: Calculates the running sum of the points.
transform.scalar: Returns the query's points if it returns exactly one series.
transform.sgn: Returns 1 for each positive point, -1 for each negative one and 0 for zero.
transform.sin: Returns the sine of each point.
transform.sinh: Returns the hyperbolic sine of each point.
transform.smooth-exponential: Smooths the points with an exponential moving average using the given factor.
transform.sort: Sorts the series by their last point in ascending order.
transform.sort-desc: Sorts the series by their last point in descending order.
transform.sqrt: Returns the square root of each point.
transform.start: Returns the timestamp of the first point, in seconds.
transform.step: Returns the step between points, in seconds.
transform.tan: Returns the tangent of each point.
transform.tanh: Returns the hyperbolic tangent of each point.
transform.time: Returns the timestamp of each point, in seconds.
transform.timezone-offset: Returns the offset of the given time zone from UTC, in seconds.
transform.ttf: Estimates how many seconds remain until the free resources run out.
transform.union: Returns the series of all the given queries together.
transform.year: Returns the year of each point.

label.alias: Sets the given name on every series.
label.drop-common-labels: Drops the labels whose values are the same in every series.
label.label-copy: Copies the values of labels to other labels.
label.label-graphite-group: Replaces the metric name with the given parts of its Graphite name, joined with dots.
label.label-join: Joins the values of labels with the given separator into another label.
label.label-keep: Deletes all labels except the given ones.
label.label-lowercase: Lowercases the values of the given labels.
label.label-map: Maps the values of a label to new values.
label.label-match: Keeps the series whose label matches the given regular expression.
label.label-mismatch: Drops the series whose label matches the given regular expression.
label.label-move: Moves the values of labels to other labels.
label.label-replace: Stores the replacement in another label when a label matches the given regular expression.
label.label-set: Sets the given labels to the given values.
label.label-transform: Replaces every match of the given regular expression in a label's value.
label.label-uppercase: Uppercases the values of the given labels.
label.label-value: Returns the numeric value of the given label.
label.labels-equal: Keeps the series in which the listed labels have the same value.
label.sort-by-label: Sorts the series by the given labels in ascending order.
label.sort-by-label-desc: Sorts the series by the given labels in descending order.
label.sort-by-label-numeric: Sorts the series by the given labels as numbers in ascending order.
label.sort-by-label-numeric-desc: Sorts the series by the given labels as numbers in descending order.

aggregate.bottomk: Returns up to the given number of points with the smallest values.
aggregate.bottomk-avg: Returns up to the given number of series with the smallest averages.
aggregate.bottomk-last: Returns up to the given number of series with the smallest last values.
aggregate.bottomk-max: Returns up to the given number of series with the smallest maximums.
aggregate.bottomk-median: Returns up to the given number of series with the smallest medians.
aggregate.bottomk-min: Returns up to the given number of series with the smallest minimums.
aggregate.count: Counts the non-empty points per group.
aggregate.count-values: Counts the points with the same value, one series per value under the given label.
aggregate.distinct: Counts the unique values per group.
aggregate.geomean: Calculates the geometric mean per group.
aggregate.histogram: Builds a VictoriaMetrics histogram per group.
aggregate.limitk: Returns up to the given number of series per group.
aggregate.mad: Calculates the median absolute deviation per group.
aggregate.max: Returns the biggest value per group.
aggregate.min: Returns the smallest value per group.
aggregate.mode: Returns the most frequent value per group.
aggregate.outliers-iqr: Returns the series with at least one point outside the interquartile range.
aggregate.outliers-mad: Returns the series with at least one point farther from the median than the given multiple of the median absolute deviation.
aggregate.outliersk: Returns up to the given number of series with the biggest standard deviation.
aggregate.quantile: Calculates the given quantile per group.
aggregate.quantiles: Calculates several quantiles per group, one series per quantile under the given label.
aggregate.share: Returns each point's share of its group's sum, from 0 to 1.
aggregate.stddev: Calculates the standard deviation per group.
aggregate.sum2: Sums the squares of the values per group.
aggregate.topk: Returns up to the given number of points with the biggest values.
aggregate.topk-avg: Returns up to the given number of series with the biggest averages.
aggregate.topk-last: Returns up to the given number of series with the biggest last values.
aggregate.topk-max: Returns up to the given number of series with the biggest maximums.
aggregate.topk-median: Returns up to the given number of series with the biggest medians.
aggregate.topk-min: Returns up to the given number of series with the biggest minimums.
aggregate.zscore: Calculates the z-score of each value within its group.

loki.json: Extracts the fields of a JSON line. Nested keys are joined with an underscore.
loki.logfmt: Extracts the key=value pairs of a logfmt line.
loki.regexp: Extracts the named groups of a regular expression as fields.
loki.pattern: Extracts fields by matching each line against a pattern of literal text and named captures.
loki.unpack: Unpacks a JSON line made by a pack stage, restoring the labels packed into it.
loki.line-format: Rewrites each line from a template that can use its labels and fields.
loki.label-format: Renames labels, or sets them from a template.
loki.drop: Removes the listed labels and fields.
loki.keep: Keeps only the listed labels and fields, and removes the rest.
loki.decolorize: Removes ANSI color codes from each line.
loki.contains: Keeps the lines that contain the text.
loki.not-contains: Drops the lines that contain the text.
loki.matches: Keeps the lines that match the regular expression.
loki.not-matches: Drops the lines that match the regular expression.
loki.label: Stream label. Loki indexes it, so a filter on it is fast.
loki.field: Field found in the log lines. Loki does not index it, so a filter on it reads every line of the selected streams.

sql.from: Start of the selected time range in unix milliseconds
sql.to: End of the selected time range in unix milliseconds
sql.interval: Auto-calculated interval based on time range and resolution (ex. "15s", "5m", "1h")
sql.range: Length of the selected time range in whole seconds (ex. "3600s")
sql.range-s: Length of the selected time range in seconds
sql.range-ms: Length of the selected time range in milliseconds
sql.unix-epoch-from: Start of the selected time range as a unix epoch timestamp (in seconds)
sql.unix-epoch-to: End of the selected time range as a unix epoch timestamp (in seconds)
sql.unix-epoch-nano-from: Start of the selected time range as a unix epoch timestamp (in nanoseconds)
sql.unix-epoch-nano-to: End of the selected time range as a unix epoch timestamp (in nanoseconds)

victorialogs.label: Stream field. A stream filter on it selects logs quickly.

fields.stream: The stream of the log, written as its stream fields.
fields.stream-id: The unique ID of the log's stream.

pipes.block-stats: Returns storage stats for each field in every data block the query reads.
pipes.blocks-count: Counts the data blocks the query reads.
pipes.coalesce: Stores the first non-empty value of the listed fields in one field.
pipes.collapse-nums: Replaces the decimal and hexadecimal numbers in a field with a placeholder.
pipes.decolorize: Removes ANSI color codes from a field, or from the message by default.
pipes.drop-empty-fields: Removes fields with empty values, and logs left with no fields.
pipes.extract: Extracts text from a field into new fields, using a pattern.
pipes.extract-regexp: Extracts the named groups of a regular expression into fields.
pipes.facets: Returns the most frequent values of every field, with an estimated log count.
pipes.field-names: Returns the field names of the logs, with an estimated log count for each.
pipes.field-values: Returns the values of a field, with the number of logs for each.
pipes.filter: Keeps the logs that match a filter.
pipes.first: Sorts the logs by the given fields and returns the first N.
pipes.format: Builds a field from a pattern that can use other fields.
pipes.generate-sequence: Replaces the results with N logs, whose messages count up from 0.
pipes.hash: Stores an integer hash of a field.
pipes.join: Joins the logs with the results of another query, by the given fields.
pipes.json-array-concat: Joins the items of a JSON array into one string.
pipes.json-array-len: Stores the length of a JSON array.
pipes.last: Sorts the logs by the given fields and returns the last N.
pipes.len: Stores the byte length of a field.
pipes.math: Calculates new fields from numeric fields.
pipes.pack-json: Packs the fields of each log into a JSON object, stored in one field.
pipes.pack-logfmt: Packs the fields of each log into a logfmt message, stored in one field.
pipes.query-stats: Returns execution stats of the query, such as the bytes it read.
pipes.replace: Replaces a substring in a field.
pipes.replace-regexp: Replaces the text matching a regular expression in a field.
pipes.running-stats: Adds running stats, such as a running count or sum, to each log.
pipes.sample: Returns a random sample of one log in every N.
pipes.set-stream-fields: Sets the listed fields as the stream fields of each log.
pipes.sort: Sorts the logs by the given fields.
pipes.split: Splits a field by a separator into a JSON array.
pipes.stats: Calculates stats over the logs, optionally grouped by fields or time buckets.
pipes.stats-remote: Like stats, but returns intermediate state in place of final values.
pipes.stream-context: Adds the logs before and after each match in its stream.
pipes.time-add: Adds a duration to the time of each log.
pipes.top: Returns the most frequent values of the given fields, with their log counts.
pipes.total-stats: Adds stats over all the logs, such as a total count or sum, to each log.
pipes.union: Appends the results of another query.
pipes.uniq: Returns the unique values of the given fields.
pipes.unpack-json: Extracts the keys of a JSON field into fields.
pipes.unpack-logfmt: Extracts the key=value pairs of a logfmt field into fields.
pipes.unpack-syslog: Extracts the parts of a syslog message into fields.
pipes.unpack-words: Extracts the words of a field into a JSON array.
pipes.unroll: Turns the JSON arrays in the given fields into separate logs.

filters.contains-all: Matches logs that contain all the given words or phrases.
filters.contains-any: Matches logs that contain at least one of the given words or phrases.
filters.contains-common-case: Matches logs that contain the phrases in their common uppercase and lowercase forms.
filters.eq-field: Matches logs where this field equals another field.
filters.equals-common-case: Matches logs where the field equals the phrases in their common uppercase and lowercase forms.
filters.exact: Matches logs whose value is exactly this text.
filters.i: Makes a word, phrase or prefix match in any case.
filters.in: Matches logs whose value is one of the given values, or is returned by a subquery.
filters.ipv4-range: Matches IPv4 addresses in the given range.
filters.ipv6-range: Matches IPv6 addresses in the given range.
filters.json-array-contains-any: Matches JSON arrays that hold at least one of the given values.
filters.le-field: Matches logs where this field does not exceed another field.
filters.len-range: Matches logs whose value length is in the given range.
filters.lt-field: Matches logs where this field is smaller than another field.
filters.pattern-match: Matches a pattern with placeholders, such as one for a number or an IP, anywhere in the value.
filters.pattern-match-full: Matches a pattern with placeholders, such as one for a number or an IP, against the whole value.
filters.pattern-match-prefix: Matches a pattern with placeholders, such as one for a number or an IP, at the start of the value.
filters.pattern-match-suffix: Matches a pattern with placeholders, such as one for a number or an IP, at the end of the value.
filters.range: Matches numeric values in the given range.
filters.seq: Matches logs that contain the given words or phrases in that order.
filters.string-range: Matches string values in the given range.
filters.value-type: Matches logs whose field is stored with the given type.

stats.any: Returns a sample value of the field.
stats.avg: Calculates the average of the numeric values.
stats.count: Counts the logs. With fields, counts the logs where at least one of them is not empty.
stats.count-empty: Counts the logs where the listed fields are empty.
stats.count-uniq: Counts the unique non-empty values of the listed fields.
stats.count-uniq-hash: Counts unique values by their hash. It is faster and uses less memory, but it can undercount.
stats.field-max: Returns a field from the log with the largest value in another field.
stats.field-min: Returns a field from the log with the smallest value in another field.
stats.histogram: Returns histogram buckets for a field.
stats.json-values: Packs the given fields of each log into a JSON array.
stats.max: Returns the largest value of the listed fields.
stats.median: Estimates the median of the listed fields.
stats.min: Returns the smallest value of the listed fields.
stats.quantile: Estimates a quantile, from 0 to 1, of the listed fields.
stats.rate: Calculates the average number of logs per second over the time range.
stats.rate-sum: Calculates the average per-second rate of the sum of numeric fields.
stats.row-any: Returns any one log of the group as JSON.
stats.row-max: Returns the log with the largest value of a field, as JSON.
stats.row-min: Returns the log with the smallest value of a field, as JSON.
stats.stddev: Calculates the standard deviation of the numeric values.
stats.sum-len: Adds up the byte lengths of the values.
stats.uniq-values: Returns the unique non-empty values as a sorted JSON array.
stats.values: Returns all the values, empty ones included, as a JSON array.

running-stats.count: The number of logs so far.
running-stats.first: The value of the field in the earliest log.
running-stats.last: The value of the field in the latest log so far.
running-stats.sum: The sum of the numeric values so far.

total-stats.first: The value of the field in the earliest log.
total-stats.last: The value of the field in the latest log.
total-stats.max: The largest value across all the logs.
total-stats.min: The smallest value across all the logs.
total-stats.sum: The sum of the numeric values across all the logs.

math.ceil: Rounds up to the nearest integer.
math.exp: Raises e to the given power.
math.floor: Rounds down to the nearest integer.
math.max: Returns the largest of the given values.
math.min: Returns the smallest of the given values.
math.now: Returns the current Unix timestamp in nanoseconds.
math.rand: Returns a random number from 0 up to, but not including, 1.
math.round: Rounds to an integer, or to the nearest multiple of a second argument.
